Definition: Does the register cover births, deaths and marriages?
Comments: Civil Registry Act 2018 covers births, deaths, marriages per snippets and standard CRVS.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The Civil Registry Act 2018 legally covers births, deaths, marriages and divorce, but a 2024 conference presentation by the Director General of the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration confirms the Act's regulations remain only 'partially developed' and operationalisation is delayed by budgetary constraints and 'limited ICT infrastructure'; a 2021 UNICEF-commissioned assessment separately found the only digital element (a birth notification system run with the Ministry of Health) had been non-operational since 2018. No evidence of digital death, marriage or divorce registration was found. Because the variable asks about digital capture rather than legal scope, downgraded from 3 (All) to 2 (Some).

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Birth registration completeness 35.5% per UNSD 2019 data, falls in 20-49% range.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original UNSD spreadsheet link is now dead (fetch failed with CRAWL_UNEXPECTED_CONTENT_TYPE). UNICEF's October 2022 'Statistical Update on Birth Registration in Africa' still cites 34-35% birth registration completeness for South Sudan, sourced from the 2010 South Sudan Household Survey — no more recent nationally representative survey was found, and UNICEF's own country page corroborates roughly 35% registered / 65% undocumented. Confirmed at 2 (20-49%); note the underlying survey data is now 15 years old and a fresher national survey is needed.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital electoral register?
Comments: Electoral register maintained by NEC; biometric verification machines received 2025 for 2026 elections (under development/planned digital).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original Facebook source is in fact a Ugandan NBS Television post (comments reference Ugandan politics), unrelated to South Sudan and unusable. Fresh 2025-2026 reporting confirms South Sudan's National Elections Commission had, as of late June 2026, not yet launched voter registration for the 22 December 2026 elections (Pan African Visions: 'major preparations, including voter registration, have yet to begin'), was only just releasing US$1m in June 2026 to build registration infrastructure, and had tendered for biometric registration kits in February 2025; the prior (2010) constituency boundaries are being reused in the absence of a census. This is consistent with 'Under development' (3) rather than a deployed register — confirmed at 3, but flag for human review as the status could shift quickly once registration begins.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the business register?
Comments: TIN registration requires Certificate of Incorporation; likely linked/under development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source page returned no substantive content on fetch (effectively dead). Direct verification of the NRA eTax platform confirms that businesses must first be validated at the Ministry of Justice's e-business portal (business.eservices.gov.ss) before a TIN is issued, and the Ministry of Justice's Directorate of Registration of Businesses, Associations and NGOs explicitly states it 'approves validation of businesses and company information for e-tax purposes before issuance of TIN'. This is an operating (if manual/procedural rather than fully automated) linkage between the two registers, not merely a plan. Upgraded from 3 (Under development) to 4 (Partially integrated).
